q: So we had a two week break from our daycare and since they don’t potty train I decided this was the time to potty train! I’m a teacher with summers off so I was able to stay home while the daycare was closed.
cx: Teacher-parent of a 22-month-old times Oh Crap to a daycare closure.

q: day 1 was no pants and a lot of cleaning up pee off the floor. It was so stressful and tiring. I felt like I couldn’t relax and was trying to find every little cue and give him success.

q: he doesn’t pee with the daycare people. They are very kind and patient with him but my son has been having tearful drop offs I think because he doesn’t like holding it all day :(

q: I wish I had been more chilled and relaxed when I started potty training but it was extremely anxiety producing for the first few days and I wish I had handled my own vibes better.
cx: Same parent a month in, looking back on the start.

q: With us, my son is very cup trained. I bought a collapsible silicon cup for my bag that takes no space, and at home we have the clear solo cups.
cx: Same parent on the cup workaround taken from the method.

q: about 2 weeks ago I’ve been preaching with/to her saying “I am Brave, I am Strong, I am Beautiful”. She would do this through tears, and I would emphasize how she needs to believe, say it like she means it.
cx: Same father on the phrase that broke weeks of bedtime panic.

q: We’re 3 nights in a row of no issues, last night we just did our regular routine and right to bed instead of the hour to 2 hour long ordeal.
cx: Same father, a few nights in.

q: I can safely say that the oh crap method has successfully worked for my four year-old-  for the last three days he had no accidents and uses the potty without being reminded to.
cx: Parent who waited until age four reports day 12 of the method.

q: I also have gone through some bad injuries and have been in a wheelchair on and off since he was 2. I had posted that he was stubborn and that I had not had it in me to potty train him before now and received a couple of judgemental comments about that- just know that only \*you\* really understand your child and your circumstances.
cx: Same parent on judgement for training late while using a wheelchair.

q: Most of us are already very hard on ourselves and come to subreddits like this for support, not snarky commentary.
cx: Same parent on the judgemental comments.

q: We have been stuck in blocks 2-3 of Oh Crap (pants on but commando, short outings away from home) for almost a month now and I was feeling so defeated.  I know the author doesn't promise success in '3 days' or offer much of a specific timeframe, but I still felt like a failure because so many people online seem to say they potty trained within a week or two even at this younger age.
cx: Mother of a strong-willed 22-month-old stuck mid-method for a month.

q: We went out to a playgroup this morning and I decided for both of our sanity, I would just let her wear a nappy again.
cx: Same mother on the day she stopped prompting; the child told her before peeing.

q: The nappy didn't ruin anything and she self-initiated AND held her pee without any prompting from me at all.  Maybe I just need to drop the rope and accept that it will mean we continue having some accidents and may be using some nappies for a while longer
I've been so scared of reverting back to any kind of nappy during the day in case of 'confusion' or her not feeling as wet.
cx: Same mother on the fear the method gave her.

q: his first year of life was basically the worst year of mine. He was colicky, he was frustrated and angry all the time.
cx: Parent of a 15-month-old who changed once he started walking.
